ruedas.what_es: Seis ruedas de aluminio, cada una con su propio motor. Llevan el rover sobre arena y rocas filosas. Son más resistentes que las de Curiosity.
ruedas.what_en: Six aluminum wheels, each with its own motor. They carry the rover over sand and sharp rocks, and are tougher than Curiosity's wheels.

facts.quote: 20.7 inches (52.5 centimeters) in diameter
Perseverance has six wheels, each with its own motor.
Each wheel has an aggressive tread with 48 grousers (or cleats), machined into its surface.

heritage.note_es: Las ruedas se rediseñaron a partir de las de Curiosity, que se desgastaron con rocas filosas: son más angostas, más grandes y de aluminio más grueso.
heritage.note_en: The wheels were redesigned from Curiosity's, which wore down on sharp rocks: narrower, larger in diameter and thicker aluminum.
heritage.quote: Perseverance's wheels are narrower, with a bigger diameter and thicker aluminum.

suspension.what_es: Sistema de brazos articulados que une las ruedas al cuerpo. Mantiene todas las ruedas en el suelo y deja pasar sobre rocas sin volcarse.
suspension.what_en: A system of pivoting arms linking the wheels to the body. It keeps all wheels on the ground and lets the rover roll over rocks without tipping.

facts.quote: Perseverance is designed to withstand a 45-degree tilt in any direction without tipping over.
Its top speed on flat, hard ground is just under 0.1 mph (152 meters per hour).

facts.value_es: Tan grandes como una rueda (52,5 cm)
facts.value_en: As large as a wheel (52.5 cm)
facts.quote: drive over obstacles (such as rocks) or through depressions as large as the rover's wheel (20.7 inches, or 52.5 centimeters)

heritage.note_es: El rocker-bogie voló por primera vez en Marte en el pequeño rover Sojourner.
heritage.note_en: The rocker-bogie first flew on Mars on the small Sojourner rover.

heritage.note_es: Se eligió de nuevo el rocker-bogie por su larga trayectoria, con una versión más ligera.
heritage.note_en: Chosen again for its long track record, in a lighter version.

source.title: NTRS: The Challenges of Designing the Rocker-Bogie Suspension for the Mars Exploration Rover

heritage.quote: the use of a rocker-bogie suspension was the obvious choice due to its extensive heritage

heritage.note_en: Curiosity also uses a rocker-bogie suspension.
heritage.quote: Geology lab, rocker-bogie suspension, rock-vaporizing laser and lots of cameras

cuerpo.what_es: La caja caliente de electrónica (WEB) protege y mantiene a temperatura los computadores del rover. Hay dos computadores idénticos, para tener siempre uno de repuesto.
cuerpo.what_en: The warm electronics box (WEB) protects the rover's computers and keeps them at a safe temperature. There are two identical computers so one is always a spare.

facts.value_es: 3 m de largo, 2,7 m de ancho, 2,2 m de alto
facts.value_en: 10 ft (3 m) long, 9 ft (2.7 m) wide, 7 ft (2.2 m) tall
facts.quote: Length 10 feet (3 meters) Width 9 feet (2.7 meters) Height 7 feet (2.2 meters)
Weight/mass 2,260 pounds / 1,025 kilograms
Radiation-hardened central processor with PowerPC 750 Architecture: a BAE RAD 750

heritage.note_es: Perseverance parte de la configuración de Curiosity, con una caja de herramientas científicas y tecnológicas añadida.
heritage.note_en: Perseverance starts from Curiosity's configuration, with an added science and technology toolbox.
heritage.quote: is based on the Mars Science Laboratory's Curiosity rover configuration, with an added science and technology toolbox.

mastil.what_es: Mástil que da al rover una vista a escala humana. En la cabeza lleva SuperCam y las dos Mastcam-Z; las cámaras de navegación van a los lados.
mastil.what_en: A mast that gives the rover a human-scale view. The head carries SuperCam and two Mastcam-Z cameras, with the Navcams on the sides.

source.title: Bell et al. 2021, Space Science Reviews (PMC)

facts.quote: Mastcam-Z consists of a pair of focusable, 4:1 zoomable cameras
from a distance of more than 20 feet (7 meters)

facts.value_es: Ven una pelota de golf a 25 m
facts.value_en: See a golf ball from 25 m (82 ft)
facts.quote: these cameras can see an object as small as a golf ball from 82 feet (25 meters) away.

heritage.note_es: Mastcam-Z se basa directamente en las Mastcam de Curiosity y suma zoom 4:1.
heritage.note_en: Mastcam-Z is based directly on Curiosity's Mastcam and adds a 4:1 zoom.

source.title: Bell et al. 2021, Space Science Reviews (PMC)

heritage.quote: Mastcam-Z is a high-heritage imaging system based directly on the successful MSL Mastcam investigation

heritage.note_es: SuperCam es el sucesor de ChemCam: dos de sus espectrómetros son casi idénticos a los de ChemCam, y suma técnicas nuevas.
heritage.note_en: SuperCam builds on ChemCam: two of its spectrometers are nearly identical to ChemCam's, and it adds new techniques.

source.title: Wiens et al. 2021, Space Science Reviews (Springer)

heritage.quote: nearly identical to their counterparts on ChemCam

brazo.what_es: Brazo que se mueve como el tuyo, con hombro, codo y muñeca. Sostiene las herramientas de la torreta para sacar muestras y analizar rocas.
brazo.what_en: An arm that moves much like yours, with shoulder, elbow and wrist. It holds the turret tools that drill cores and analyze rocks.

facts.quote: The 7-foot-long (2.1 meters) robotic arm can move a lot like your arm.
There are five degrees of freedom, made possible by tiny rotary actuator motors.

torreta.what_es: La "mano" del brazo. Lleva el taladro de muestras y los instrumentos PIXL, SHERLOC y WATSON para ver y analizar rocas muy de cerca.
torreta.what_en: The arm's "hand". It carries the sample drill plus the PIXL, SHERLOC and WATSON instruments for close-up views and analysis of rocks.

facts.value_es: SHERLOC, WATSON, PIXL, GDRT, sensor de contacto, taladro
facts.value_en: SHERLOC, WATSON, PIXL, GDRT, ground contact sensor, drill
facts.quote: SHERLOC and WATSON, PIXL, GDRT (Gaseous Dust Removal Tool), Ground Contact Sensor, Drill
Diameter of drilled holes 1 inch (27 millimeters)

facts.value_es: Brocas de núcleo, de regolito y un abrasivo
facts.value_en: Coring bits, regolith bits and an abrader
facts.quote: A suite of interchangeable bits: coring bits, regolith bits and an abrader.

heritage.note_es: La torreta de Perseverance es más grande que la de Curiosity, para llevar el taladro de núcleos y más instrumentos.
heritage.note_en: Perseverance's turret is larger than Curiosity's, to hold the coring drill and more instruments.
heritage.quote: the rover has a larger "hand," or turret at the end of the robot arm.

rtg.what_es: Una batería nuclear. Convierte en electricidad el calor de la desintegración natural del plutonio. También da calor para mantener tibias las herramientas del rover.
rtg.what_en: A nuclear battery. It turns the heat of plutonium's natural radioactive decay into electricity, and its heat keeps the rover's tools at working temperature.

facts.quote: Uses 10.6 pounds (4.8 kilograms) of plutonium dioxide as the source of the steady supply of heat

facts.value_es: Unos 110 W al lanzamiento, baja unos pocos por ciento al año
facts.value_en: About 110 W at launch, declining a few percent per year
facts.quote: About 110 watts at launch, declining a few percent per year
has a 14-year operational lifetime

heritage.note_es: Curiosity fue el primer uso del MMRTG.
heritage.note_en: Curiosity was the first use of the MMRTG.
heritage.quote: NASA's Curiosity rover was launched carrying an MMRTG as its source of electrical power on November 26, 2011

heritage.note_es: Dragonfly usará un MMRTG, del mismo tipo que los de Curiosity y Perseverance (lanzamiento previsto, no antes de julio de 2028).
heritage.note_en: Dragonfly will use an MMRTG, a similar type to those on Curiosity and Perseverance (planned launch, no earlier than July 2028).

source.title: Dragonfly: Spacecraft and Instruments - NASA Science

heritage.quote: Dragonfly will use an MMRTG (Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator), a similar type of fuel source as the ones used

antenas.what_es: Tres antenas en la cubierta del rover. Una habla con la Tierra a mayor velocidad, otra recibe órdenes y otra envía datos a orbitadores de Marte.
antenas.what_en: Three antennas on the rover's deck. One talks to Earth at higher speed, one receives commands, and one sends data through Mars orbiters.

facts.quote: Up to 2 megabits per second on the rover-to-orbiter relay link.
Hexagonally shaped, 1 foot (0.3 meters) in diameter
Approximately 10 bits per second or faster from the Deep Space Network's 112-foot-diameter (34-meter-diameter) antennas

hazcams.what_es: Seis cámaras que vigilan el camino adelante y atrás. Detectan rocas grandes, zanjas y dunas para que el rover decida por dónde ir.
hazcams.what_en: Six cameras that watch the path ahead and behind. They spot large rocks, trenches and dunes so the rover can decide where to drive.

facts.value_es: 6: cuatro al frente y dos atrás
facts.value_en: 6: four in front, two at the rear
facts.quote: Perseverance carries six newly developed Hazard Detection Cameras (HazCams): four in front and two on the rear.

facts.value_en: Large rocks, trenches and sand dunes
facts.quote: HazCams detect hazards to the front and back pathways of the rover, such as large rocks, trenches, and sand dunes.

rimfax.what_es: Un radar que usa ondas de radio para mirar bajo el suelo, debajo del rover. Muestra capas de roca y suelo que no se ven en la superficie.
rimfax.what_en: A radar that uses radio waves to look into the ground beneath the rover. It reveals rock and soil layers you cannot see on the surface.

facts.quote: Less than 6.6 pounds (3 kilograms)
Power 5 to 10 watts

source.title: Hamran et al. 2020, Space Science Reviews (Springer)

facts.quote: The operating frequency range of 150–1200 MHz covers the typical frequencies of GPR used in geology.

heritage.note_es: Una versión de banda ultraancha de este radar fue prototipo del radar WISDOM del rover europeo ExoMars (lanzamiento previsto a fines de 2028).
heritage.note_en: An ultra-wideband version of this radar was a prototype for the WISDOM radar on ESA's ExoMars rover (launch planned late 2028).

source.title: Hamran et al. 2020, Space Science Reviews (Springer)

heritage.quote: Later and ultra wideband version was developed as a prototype for the WISDOM radar on the ExoMars mission

missions.name: Mars 2020 (Perseverance)
missions.summary_es: Rover de NASA que busca señales de vida antigua en Marte. Recoge núcleos de roca y regolito para una posible misión futura que los traiga a la Tierra.
missions.summary_en: NASA rover searching for signs of ancient life on Mars. It collects rock and regolith cores for a possible future mission to bring them to Earth.

milestones.text_es: Aterrizaje en el cráter Jezero, Marte.
Primer vuelo de Ingenuity: el primer vuelo controlado y con motor en otro planeta.
milestones.text_en: Ingenuity's first flight: the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.
milestones.quote: On April 19, 2021, NASA's Ingenuity Mars Helicopter made history when it completed the first powered, controlled flight on the Red Planet.

milestones.text_es: Se sella la primera muestra de núcleo de roca (muestra n.º 2; la n.º 1 fue de atmósfera, sellada el 6 de agosto de 2021).
milestones.text_en: First rock-core sample sealed (sample No. 2; sample No. 1 was atmospheric, sealed Aug. 6, 2021).
milestones.quote: Sample No. 2 Feature Name: Rochette Sample Type: Rock Core Sol Sealed: 194 Date Sealed: Sept. 6, 2021

milestones.text_es: Último vuelo de Ingenuity (72 vuelos en total); su misión terminó el 25 de enero de 2024.
milestones.text_en: Ingenuity's last flight (72 flights in total); its mission ended Jan. 25, 2024.
milestones.quote: Ingenuity flew for the last time on January 18, 2024, and completed its mission on January 25, 2024

milestones.text_es: Estado actual: la página de NASA la clasifica como misión activa (consultada el 22 de noviembre de 2026).
milestones.text_en: Current status: NASA's page lists it as an active mission (checked Nov. 22, 2026).

notes: Years for heritage entries are launch years: Curiosity 2011 (source: NASA Curiosity page, 'launched in 2011'; RPS FAQ gives Nov. 26, 2011), Sojourner/Mars Pathfinder 1996 (NSSDCA launch date 1996-12-04), MER 2004 is the LANDING year (NASA MER page: 'landed on the Red Planet in 2004'). Dragonfly 2028 is a planned launch ('NET July 2028' on science.nasa.gov/mission/dragonfly/), not confirmed; the MMRTG quote is from the spacecraft page, the date from the mission page. RIMFAX/WISDOM 2028 is a planned launch from ESA (https://explorationscience.esa.int/project/exomars-rosalind-franklin-rfm/: 'launch is scheduled for late 2028'); the Springer paper itself still says 2022. Quotes are whitespace-normalized from the page text; table values on NASA pages (e.g. 'Length 10 feet ...') are joined label+value. Body dimensions/mass are the rover totals shown in the Body table. The first-sample milestone uses NASA's sample list: No. 1 Roubion atmospheric sealed Aug. 6, 2021; No. 2 first rock core sealed Sept. 6, 2021. Odometer omitted from milestones: main page says 'On Oct. 11, its odometer reached 28.10 miles (45.22 kilometers)' (2026, past Opportunity's record) and page last updated Oct. 14, 2026; usable as 'as of Oct. 11, 2026'. Not verified / left empty: heritage for arm, antennas, HazCams (NASA calls them 'newly developed'), Navcams; Viking SNAP-19 ancestor of MMRTG is verified (RPS pages) but no launch year read, so omitted. Rover wheel diameter appears as 52.5 cm in the spec table and 52.6 cm in a caption; 52.5 used. Mastcam-Z/SuperCam papers are peer-reviewed (Space Science Reviews). Spirit/Opportunity computer comparison ('10 times the speed') is not used as heritage.
